blocks.text: NASL has built a digital twin of Shaddad, its tracked autonomous agricultural platform, as the MATLAB R2026b project `Shaddad_UGV` in Simulink and Simscape. The top model `Shaddad_System` links the STM32H743 main-controller firmware model (`Shaddad_MCU`), the STM32G4 BMS ECU model (`Shaddad_BMS`) and the physical plant (`Shaddad_Plant`): a 48 V LiFePO4 pack, the hard-wired safety chain, two PMSM traction drives with 24:1 gearboxes and the tracks on soil. Build scripts (`scripts/build/build_*.m`) generate every model, and parameter files (`params/param_*.m`) supply all values, so the twin is reproducible.

This report demonstrates Phase 1: a simulated operator drives the robot over the SBUS remote-control link, from transmitter to tracks. In nine scenarios, 64 of 71 criteria pass, 6 fail and 1 is blocked because Accelerator mode is unavailable on the reference PC ({tab:tab_front_keys}). Power-up, RC driving, corrupted-frame rejection and the front E-stop meet every motion, latency and safety criterion: a transmitter frame reaches the CAN drive command within 28 ms, and the E-stop removes motor torque in 15 ms. The failures are deceleration overshoots in three stop scenarios (0.9-9.7 % above the limit) and three criteria on a 20° slope with the full sprayer.

blocks.text: This document serves two purposes. It is the **Phase 1 demonstration report** for the Shaddad UGV digital twin: it describes what the model contains and records the evidence that the model operates the robot under SBUS remote control, with measured results against the acceptance criteria. It is also the **user manual**: it shows an engineer how to open the project, drive the simulated robot, run the acceptance scenarios, read the results and change the model safely. Because the requirements of the model follow from the work Shaddad does for NASL's customers, the report starts by explaining what Shaddad is and what its job is.

The report covers Phase 1, SBUS remote-control operation, in the simulation target. {tab:tab_front_scope} lists what is covered in full, what appears only as an outlook, and what was not demonstrated.

items: **Units.** SI units throughout (m, s, m/s, rad/s, N m, A, V, Wh). Angles are in rad in the model; deg is used where stated.
**Frames and signs.** World frame ENU, body frame FLU (forward-left-up) on every bus. A positive yaw rate turns the robot left, so a right steer gives a negative yaw rate (S1: -0.350 rad/s).

**Names.** `Monospace` marks MATLAB commands, files, models, blocks, buses and signals. Paths are relative to the project root, written `<project root>` in commands ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Getting the project}).
**Notation.** Text and tables use m/s², ≤, ≥, ±, Ω, °C and 20°; the ASCII forms appear only in code and console excerpts.

**Criterion status.** PASS: measured and within the limit. FAIL: measured and outside the limit. BLOCKED: cannot be evaluated in this environment, for example because it needs Accelerator mode or Simulink Coder.

**Figures.** Simulink diagrams are printed from the models (`print -s`); a large diagram appears as an overview with numbered callouts and as a detail crop in which block names print at 6 pt or more. Window captures have their title bars cropped. A caption states when a diagram was re-arranged for legibility.
**Open items.** Unknown or unconfirmed values are marked [TBD - <source>].
